observations: Four completed exterior photographs show two narrow recessed upper window bands, three-row solid/perforated cladding bands, regular panel joints and a tall ground-floor fin screen.
The close frontal photograph supports the distinction between solid upper panels and subtly perforated panels immediately above the glazing; a single flat grey material would lose this detail.
The exterior corners continue window bands around both sides. Window mullions and opaque infill vary within the band.
Facade photograph GARC_05 includes the older PhysicsI building to the left, independently supporting adjacency.
Campus and local site plans identify the courtyard block north of PhysicsI and west of P1.
Close exterior images GARC_08 and GARC_09 resolve perforated panels directly above the narrow glazing strips. GARC_10 resolves zinc-like mottled finish and projecting fins.

In GARC_17, the courtyard exterior visible through the foreground glazing has taller window panes, dark spandrels and slim vertical mullions. Its appearance differs from the outer metal facade. Only that background exterior informs reconstruction; no interior is being modeled.
GARC_08 shows several cylindrical louvred structures. Their locations and scale have not been established; do not invent placements.

qualification: BVV establishes envelope and position. Photographs establish material character and pattern, but panel dimensions, recess depths, fin spacing, exact elevations and unphotographed courtyard/roof details still need estimation or further evidence. Do not apply an exterior fin pattern indiscriminately to courtyard walls. No interiors.
